title: Advanced Deployment: Kubernetes and Autoscaling
summary: This day covers essential concepts for building AI engineering skills.
content:
# Advanced Deployment: Kubernetes and Autoscaling

##### The rollout that took the service down for 22 minutes

A team in Bengaluru deployed a model update to their vLLM service on Kubernetes. Standard rolling update, `maxUnavailable: 25%`, three replicas.

Kubernetes terminated the first pod and started a replacement. The new pod pulled a 34 GB image, loaded weights, and captured CUDA graphs — seven minutes. Meanwhile the readiness probe failed, so Kubernetes terminated it and tried again, because the probe had a 60-second `failureThreshold` window designed for web services.

Three restart cycles later, two of three replicas were down, the remaining one was saturated, and every request was timing out.

**22 minutes of degraded service, caused entirely by probe configuration written for stateless web apps.**

The fix was four settings: a `startupProbe` with a 15-minute budget, `maxUnavailable: 0` with `maxSurge: 1`, a `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` long enough to drain in-flight generations, and a `preStop` hook.

**LLM workloads break most Kubernetes defaults**, because those defaults assume processes that start in seconds and requests that finish in milliseconds. Day 34 covered serving architecture; today is running it on Kubernetes properly.

##### What makes LLM workloads different

| Assumption in K8s defaults | Reality for LLM serving |
|---|---|
| Pods start in 5–30s | **3–10 minutes** (image pull, weight load, CUDA graphs) |
| Requests finish in ms | **Seconds to minutes** (streaming generation) |
| Scaling on CPU works | **CPU is idle; GPU is memory-bandwidth bound** |
| Nodes are interchangeable | **GPU type, count, and topology matter** |
| Images are ~200 MB | **10–40 GB** |
| Graceful shutdown is fast | **Must drain long-lived streams** |

Every one of those differences requires a configuration change.

##### Containerising a GPU workload

```dockerfile
# Multi-stage: build wheels separately, keep the runtime lean
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 AS builder

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        python3.11 python3.11-dev python3-pip build-essential git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /build
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN python3.11 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --user -r requirements.txt


FROM nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 AS runtime

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    HF_HOME=/models/.cache \
    HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
    VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        python3.11 curl libgomp1 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY --from=builder /root/.local /usr/local
COPY app/ /app/
WORKDIR /app

RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 appuser \
    && mkdir -p /models && chown -R appuser /app /models
USER appuser

EXPOSE 8000 8001
CMD ["python3.11", "-m", "vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server", \
     "--model", "/models/llama-3-8b-awq", \
     "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

**`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` is a production safeguard.** Without it, a transient Hugging Face outage or a rate limit causes your pod to fail startup — even though the weights are already on disk.

**Do not bake weights into the image.** A 34 GB image is slow to pull, expensive to store, and forces a full rebuild for a model change. Mount them instead:

```yaml
# Pre-populate a ReadOnlyMany PVC, or use an init container
initContainers:
  - name: fetch-weights
    image: your-registry/model-fetcher:v3
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
    args:
      - |
        if [ ! -f /models/llama-3-8b-awq/config.json ]; then
          aws s3 sync s3://models/llama-3-8b-awq /models/llama-3-8b-awq \
            --no-progress
        fi
    volumeMounts:
      - name: model-cache
        mountPath: /models
```

**The `if [ ! -f ... ]` guard makes restarts fast.** On a node where the volume already holds the weights, the init container exits in a second.

##### The deployment manifest

Every non-default setting here exists because of a failure mode.

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: llm-inference
  labels: {app: llm-inference, model: llama-3-8b-awq}
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0        # ← never reduce capacity during a rollout
      maxSurge: 1              # ← one extra pod at a time (GPUs are scarce)
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: llm-inference}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: llm-inference}
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "8000"
        prometheus.io/path: "/metrics"
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 180    # ← drain in-flight generations
      nodeSelector:
        cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator: nvidia-l4
      tolerations:
        - key: nvidia.com/gpu
          operator: Exists
          effect: NoSchedule
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 100
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchLabels: {app: llm-inference}
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname

      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-weights
          image: your-registry/model-fetcher:v3
          volumeMounts: [{name: model-cache, mountPath: /models}]

      containers:
        - name: vllm
          image: your-registry/llm-inference:v2026.03.14
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args:
            - --model=/models/llama-3-8b-awq
            - --quantization=awq_marlin
            - --dtype=half
            - --max-model-len=8192
            - --gpu-memory-utilization=0.90
            - --enable-prefix-caching
            - --enable-chunked-prefill
            - --max-num-seqs=128
            - --served-model-name=llama3-8b
            - --disable-log-requests

          ports:
            - {containerPort: 8000, name: http}

          resources:
            limits:
              nvidia.com/gpu: 1
              memory: 32Gi
              cpu: "8"
            requests:
              nvidia.com/gpu: 1
              memory: 32Gi
              cpu: "4"

          # THE critical fix: allow up to 15 minutes to start
          startupProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8000}
            initialDelaySeconds: 30
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 90        # 90 × 10s = 15 minutes
            timeoutSeconds: 5

          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8000}
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 3
            timeoutSeconds: 3

          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8000}
            periodSeconds: 20
            failureThreshold: 6         # tolerant — restarting costs 7 minutes
            timeoutSeconds: 10

          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                # Stop accepting new work, let in-flight requests finish
                command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 15"]

          volumeMounts:
            - {name: model-cache, mountPath: /models, readOnly: true}
            - {name: shm, mountPath: /dev/shm}

          env:
            - name: POD_NAME
              valueFrom: {fieldRef: {fieldPath: metadata.name}}
            - name: HF_HUB_OFFLINE
              value: "1"

      volumes:
        - name: model-cache
          persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: model-weights-pvc}
        - name: shm
          emptyDir: {medium: Memory, sizeLimit: 4Gi}
```

**`startupProbe` is the single most important setting.** It suspends liveness and readiness checks until startup completes, giving the pod a 15-minute budget without a permissive liveness probe forever after. This alone would have prevented the Bengaluru outage.

**`maxUnavailable: 0` with `maxSurge: 1`** means capacity never drops during a rollout. It requires one spare GPU, which is the cost of safe deployment.

**The `/dev/shm` emptyDir** is required for vLLM's multiprocessing. The Docker default of 64 MB causes cryptic crashes with tensor parallelism, and this is a frequently-hit footgun.

**A liveness probe with `failureThreshold: 6`** is deliberately tolerant. Restarting a pod costs seven minutes; a brief health-check blip should not trigger it.

**`preStop: sleep 15`** gives the endpoint controller time to remove the pod from service before the process receives SIGTERM. Without it, requests route to a terminating pod.

##### GPU scheduling and node pools

```yaml
# Node pools sized to workload class, not one pool for everything
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata: {name: gpu-quota, namespace: inference}
spec:
  hard:
    requests.nvidia.com/gpu: "24"
    limits.nvidia.com/gpu: "24"
```

```python
NODE_POOLS = {
    "inference-small": {
        "gpu": "nvidia-l4", "gpu_count": 1, "vram_gb": 24,
        "hourly_inr": 62, "min_nodes": 2, "max_nodes": 12,
        "workloads": ["llama-3-8b-awq", "embedding", "reranker"],
        "spot": False,
    },
    "inference-large": {
        "gpu": "nvidia-a100-80gb", "gpu_count": 4, "vram_gb": 320,
        "hourly_inr": 1000, "min_nodes": 1, "max_nodes": 4,
        "workloads": ["llama-3-70b-awq (TP=4)"],
        "spot": False,
    },
    "batch-spot": {
        "gpu": "nvidia-l4", "gpu_count": 1, "vram_gb": 24,
        "hourly_inr": 19, "min_nodes": 0, "max_nodes": 20,
        "workloads": ["batch-embedding", "eval-runs", "fine-tuning"],
        "spot": True,             # 70% cheaper, interruptible
    },
}
```

**Separate pools by workload class.** An 8B model on an A100-80GB wastes 56 GB; a 70B model cannot run on an L4 at all. One pool forces you to size for the largest workload.

**Spot instances for batch work only.** Interruption during interactive serving is a user-visible failure; interruption during a nightly embedding job is a retry. The 70% discount is substantial and should be captured where interruption is acceptable.

**Tensor-parallel deployments need topology awareness:**

```yaml
# TP=4 requires 4 GPUs on ONE node with NVLink — Day 9's point
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 4
nodeSelector:
  cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator: nvidia-a100-80gb
  cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator-count: "4"
```

**Never let Kubernetes split a tensor-parallel group across nodes.** The all-reduce per transformer block over Ethernet is catastrophically slow.

**GPU sharing** via time-slicing or MIG is worth knowing about:

```yaml
# MIG on A100: partition one GPU into isolated instances
nodeSelector:
  cloud.google.com/gke-gpu-partition-size: 1g.10gb
```

MIG gives hardware isolation and is suitable for small models or embedding services. Time-slicing shares without isolation and is only appropriate for development.

##### Autoscaling with KEDA

The HPA default of CPU utilisation is useless here — Day 34's point, now implemented.

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata: {name: llm-inference-scaler, namespace: inference}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {name: llm-inference}
  minReplicaCount: 2              # warm pool — never scale to zero
  maxReplicaCount: 12
  pollingInterval: 15
  cooldownPeriod: 600             # 10 min before scaling down

  advanced:
    horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig:
      behavior:
        scaleUp:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30      # react fast
          policies:
            - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
        scaleDown:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600     # ← asymmetric, deliberately
          policies:
            - {type: Pods, value: 1, periodSeconds: 300}

  triggers:
    # Primary: queue depth per replica
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
        metricName: vllm_queue_depth_per_replica
        threshold: "8"
        query: |
          sum(vllm:num_requests_waiting) /
          max(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="llm-inference"})

    # Secondary: TTFT p95 against the SLA
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
        metricName: ttft_p95_ms
        threshold: "1500"
        query: |
          histogram_quantile(0.95,
            sum(rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le)) * 1000

    # Scheduled floor for predictable IST business hours
    - type: cron
      metadata:
        timezone: Asia/Kolkata
        start: "0 9 * * 1-5"
        end: "0 20 * * 1-5"
        desiredReplicas: "6"
```

**The asymmetric stabilisation windows are the anti-flapping fix.** Scale up within 30 seconds; wait 10 minutes before scaling down. One extra replica for ten minutes costs ₹10 on an L4; a cold start during a spike costs a user-visible outage.

**The cron trigger sets a floor, not a ceiling.** Predictive scaling for known business hours plus reactive scaling for surprises handles both without exposing every spike to a multi-minute cold start.

**Cluster autoscaler configuration matters too:**

```yaml
# Give the node autoscaler time; GPU nodes take 3-5 min to provision
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: {name: cluster-autoscaler-config}
data:
  scale-down-delay-after-add: "15m"
  scale-down-unneeded-time: "15m"
  max-node-provision-time: "20m"
  expander: "least-waste"
```

##### Blue-green and canary

Day 35 covered the statistical side. Here is the Kubernetes mechanism.

```yaml
# Argo Rollouts — progressive canary with automated analysis
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata: {name: llm-inference}
spec:
  replicas: 6
  strategy:
    canary:
      canaryService: llm-inference-canary
      stableService: llm-inference-stable
      trafficRouting:
        istio:
          virtualService: {name: llm-inference-vs, routes: [primary]}

      steps:
        - setWeight: 5
        - pause: {duration: 10m}
        - analysis:
            templates: [{templateName: llm-quality-check}]
            args:
              - {name: canary-service, value: llm-inference-canary}
        - setWeight: 20
        - pause: {duration: 15m}
        - analysis:
            templates: [{templateName: llm-quality-check}]
        - setWeight: 50
        - pause: {duration: 30m}
        - analysis:
            templates: [{templateName: llm-quality-check}]
        - setWeight: 100

      analysis:
        templates: [{templateName: llm-quality-check}]
        startingStep: 2

  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: vllm
          image: your-registry/llm-inference:v2026.03.14
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata: {name: llm-quality-check}
spec:
  args: [{name: canary-service}]
  metrics:
    - name: error-rate
      interval: 2m
      count: 5
      successCondition: result[0] < 0.02
      failureLimit: 1
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
          query: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="{{args.canary-service}}",status=~"5.."}[2m]))
            / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="{{args.canary-service}}"}[2m]))

    - name: ttft-p95
      interval: 2m
      count: 5
      successCondition: result[0] < 2.0
      failureLimit: 2
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
          query: |
            histogram_quantile(0.95,
              sum(rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{service="{{args.canary-service}}"}[2m])) by (le))

    # The LLM-specific one: quality proxy, not just infrastructure
    - name: refusal-rate
      interval: 5m
      count: 3
      successCondition: result[0] < 0.15
      failureLimit: 1
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
          query: |
            sum(rate(llm_refusals_total{service="{{args.canary-service}}"}[5m]))
            / sum(rate(llm_requests_total{service="{{args.canary-service}}"}[5m]))
```

**Including a quality proxy in the analysis is what makes this an LLM canary** rather than a generic one. Error rate and latency will not detect a model update that started hallucinating — refusal rate and citation count will, as Day 35 argued.

**Blue-green is the right choice for model swaps** where you want an instant, complete cutover with a fast rollback:

```yaml
strategy:
  blueGreen:
    activeService: llm-inference-active
    previewService: llm-inference-preview
    autoPromotionEnabled: false        # require manual promotion
    scaleDownDelaySeconds: 1800        # keep the old version warm for 30 min
    prePromotionAnalysis:
      templates: [{templateName: llm-quality-check}]
```

**`scaleDownDelaySeconds: 1800` is the rollback insurance.** The previous version stays warm for thirty minutes, so a rollback is instant rather than a seven-minute cold start.

The cost is double GPU capacity during the overlap, which is real for a 70B deployment and worth it for a high-stakes change.

##### Infrastructure as code

```hcl
# terraform/gpu_cluster.tf
resource "google_container_node_pool" "inference_small" {
  name     = "inference-small"
  cluster  = google_container_cluster.primary.id
  location = var.region

  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 2
    max_node_count = 12
    location_policy = "BALANCED"
  }

  management {
    auto_repair  = true
    auto_upgrade = false        # ← manual: node upgrades evict GPU pods
  }

  node_config {
    machine_type = "g2-standard-16"
    disk_size_gb = 200
    disk_type    = "pd-ssd"     # weights load faster from SSD

    guest_accelerator {
      type  = "nvidia-l4"
      count = 1
      gpu_driver_installation_config { gpu_driver_version = "LATEST" }
    }

    labels = { workload = "llm-inference", gpu-class = "l4" }

    taint {
      key    = "nvidia.com/gpu"
      value  = "present"
      effect = "NO_SCHEDULE"
    }

    shielded_instance_config {
      enable_secure_boot          = true
      enable_integrity_monitoring = true
    }

    workload_metadata_config { mode = "GKE_METADATA" }
  }

  upgrade_settings {
    max_surge       = 1
    max_unavailable = 0
  }
}

resource "google_compute_disk" "model_weights" {
  name  = "model-weights"
  type  = "pd-ssd"
  size  = 500
  zone  = var.zone
}
```

**`auto_upgrade = false` on GPU node pools.** An automatic node upgrade evicts your pods with no coordination, and a 15-minute startup makes that a real outage. Schedule upgrades deliberately.

**`disk_type = "pd-ssd"` matters more than it looks.** Loading 35 GB of weights from a standard disk adds two to three minutes to every cold start.

##### The CI/CD pipeline

The mini project: build, test, evaluate, canary-deploy.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
name: Build and Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["app/**", "Dockerfile", "k8s/**"]

env:
  REGISTRY: asia-south1-docker.pkg.dev
  IMAGE: ${{ github.repository }}/llm-inference

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11", cache: pip}
      - run: pip install -e ".[dev]"
      - run: pytest tests/ -v --cov=app --cov-fail-under=75
      - run: ruff check app/ && mypy app/

  build:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with: {workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.WIF_PROVIDER }}}
      - id: push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          push: true
          tags: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          provenance: true          # supply-chain attestation

      - name: Scan image
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }}
          severity: CRITICAL,HIGH
          exit-code: "1"

  evaluate:
    needs: build
    runs-on: [self-hosted, gpu]        # runner with a GPU
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Start candidate service
        run: |
          docker run -d --gpus all --name candidate \
            -v /models:/models:ro -p 8000:8000 \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }}
          timeout 900 bash -c \
            'until curl -sf localhost:8000/health; do sleep 10; done'

      - name: Golden evaluation suite
        run: python -m eval.run --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 \
               --set golden --output eval/results.json

      - name: Regression gate
        run: python -m eval.gate --results eval/results.json \
               --baseline eval/baseline.json

      - name: Load test
        run: python -m bench.load --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 \
               --concurrency 64 --duration 120 \
               --assert-throughput-min 2800 --assert-ttft-p95-max 1500

  deploy:
    needs: evaluate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production          # requires approval
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: google-github-actions/get-gke-credentials@v2
        with: {cluster_name: prod, location: asia-south1}

      - name: Update rollout image
        run: |
          kubectl argo rollouts set image llm-inference \
            vllm=${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            -n inference

      - name: Watch progressive rollout
        run: |
          kubectl argo rollouts get rollout llm-inference -n inference --watch \
            --timeout 3600s

      - name: Rollback on failure
        if: failure()
        run: kubectl argo rollouts abort llm-inference -n inference
```

**The `evaluate` job runs on a GPU runner against the actual built image.** Evaluating the code without the container misses image-level problems — wrong CUDA version, missing library, changed default.

**The load-test assertions are gates, not reports.** `--assert-throughput-min 2800` fails the build if performance regressed, which catches an accidental config change that halved throughput.

##### Observability wiring

```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata: {name: llm-inference, namespace: inference}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: llm-inference}}
  endpoints:
    - {port: http, path: /metrics, interval: 15s}
---
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata: {name: llm-inference-alerts}
spec:
  groups:
    - name: llm-inference
      rules:
        - alert: LLMHighQueueDepth
          expr: sum(vllm:num_requests_waiting) / count(up{job="llm-inference"}) > 20
          for: 5m
          labels: {severity: page}
          annotations:
            summary: "Queue depth {{ $value }} per replica"
            runbook: "runbooks/llm-queue-depth.md"

        - alert: LLMHighTTFT
          expr: |
            histogram_quantile(0.95,
              sum(rate(vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 3
          for: 10m
          labels: {severity: page}
          annotations: {runbook: "runbooks/llm-latency.md"}

        - alert: LLMPodStartupSlow
          expr: |
            time() - kube_pod_created{pod=~"llm-inference-.*"} > 900
            and kube_pod_status_ready{condition="false"} == 1
          for: 2m
          labels: {severity: page}
          annotations:
            summary: "Pod {{ $labels.pod }} not ready after 15 minutes"

        - alert: GPUMemoryPressure
          expr: DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED / DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_TOTAL > 0.95
          for: 5m
          labels: {severity: warning}

        - alert: LLMQualityRegression
          expr: |
            sum(rate(llm_refusals_total[15m])) / sum(rate(llm_requests_total[15m])) > 0.15
          for: 15m
          labels: {severity: page}
          annotations:
            summary: "Refusal rate {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}"
            runbook: "runbooks/quality-regression.md"
```

**`LLMPodStartupSlow` is an LLM-specific alert** that generic Kubernetes monitoring will not have. A pod stuck past its 15-minute budget usually means a weight-loading failure, and catching it before the startup probe gives up saves a restart cycle.

**Every alert has a runbook link.** An alert without one wakes someone who then improvises.

##### Availability design

The assignment. Work backwards from the SLA.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
import math


@dataclass
class AvailabilityDesign:
    target_availability: float          # e.g. 0.995
    single_replica_availability: float = 0.99
    zones: int = 3
    cold_start_minutes: float = 7.0

    @property
    def allowed_downtime_minutes_per_month(self) -> float:
        return (1 - self.target_availability) * 30 * 24 * 60

    def replicas_needed(self) -> int:
        """P(all fail) = (1-p)^n. Solve for n."""
        p_fail = 1 - self.single_replica_availability
        target_fail = 1 - self.target_availability
        return max(2, math.ceil(math.log(target_fail) / math.log(p_fail)))

    def design(self, peak_qps: float, qps_per_replica: float) -> dict:
        capacity_replicas = math.ceil(peak_qps / qps_per_replica)
        redundancy_replicas = self.replicas_needed()
        base = max(capacity_replicas, redundancy_replicas)

        # N+1 per zone so losing a zone does not breach capacity
        per_zone = math.ceil(base / self.zones) + 1
        total = per_zone * self.zones

        return {
            "allowed_downtime_min_month": round(self.allowed_downtime_minutes_per_month, 1),
            "replicas_for_capacity": capacity_replicas,
            "replicas_for_redundancy": redundancy_replicas,
            "replicas_per_zone": per_zone,
            "total_replicas": total,
            "zone_failure_survivable": (total - per_zone) * qps_per_replica >= peak_qps,
            "warm_pool_justification": (
                f"cold start is {self.cold_start_minutes} min; reactive scaling "
                f"cannot cover a spike, so min_replicas must exceed baseline load"),
        }


design = AvailabilityDesign(target_availability=0.995)
print(design.design(peak_qps=45, qps_per_replica=12))
```

**Multi-zone is what buys you availability**, not more replicas in one zone. A zonal GPU shortage — which happens — takes out every replica in that zone simultaneously.

**Design for zone failure explicitly.** If losing one of three zones drops you below capacity, you have redundancy on paper and not in practice.

##### Common mistakes

- **No `startupProbe`** — the 22-minute outage.
- **`maxUnavailable: 25%`** on a service where each pod takes seven minutes to replace.
- **Default `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30`**, killing in-flight generations.
- **No `preStop` hook**, routing requests to terminating pods.
- **Autoscaling on CPU or GPU utilisation** rather than queue depth and TTFT.
- **Symmetric scale-up/scale-down windows**, causing flapping.
- **Scaling to zero** for interactive traffic.
- **Default `/dev/shm`** of 64 MB, crashing tensor-parallel workers.
- **Weights baked into the image**, producing 34 GB pulls.
- **`auto_upgrade = true`** on GPU node pools.
- **Tensor-parallel groups split across nodes.**
- **Canary analysis with only infrastructure metrics**, missing quality regressions.

##### Hands-on: break it, then fix it

Your practical task containerises a vLLM service and deploys it to Kubernetes with a GPU node pool and autoscaler. **Deploy first with the default probes and watch it fail** — the restart loop is instructive and takes five minutes to reproduce. Then add the `startupProbe` and see it come up cleanly. Load-test until the autoscaler triggers and confirm it scales on queue depth rather than sitting at 12% CPU.

The mini project builds the full CI/CD pipeline through canary deployment. The evaluation job on a GPU runner is the part that distinguishes this from a generic pipeline — wire the Day 36 regression gate into it so a quality regression blocks the deploy. Then push a deliberately bad model and verify the canary analysis aborts the rollout automatically.

The assignment designs a production infrastructure diagram with IaC for a given availability SLA. Show the arithmetic: allowed downtime, replicas for capacity, replicas for redundancy, per-zone distribution, and whether you survive a zone failure. Include the warm-pool justification, because "why not scale to zero" is the first question a cost-conscious reviewer will ask.

##### Key takeaways

- **`startupProbe` with a 15-minute budget is the single most important setting** — LLM pods take minutes to start, and default probes kill them mid-load.
- **`maxUnavailable: 0` with `maxSurge: 1`**, a long termination grace period, and a `preStop` hook are what make rollouts safe for long-lived streaming requests.
- **Autoscale on queue depth and TTFT with asymmetric windows** — fast up, slow down — and never scale to zero for interactive traffic.
- **Separate node pools by workload class**, keep tensor-parallel groups on one node, and use spot instances only for interruptible batch work.
- **Include a quality proxy in canary analysis.** Error rate and latency will not detect a model that started hallucinating; refusal rate will.
